title: How the thumbnail service answers a request
conclusion: Most thumbnails are cached already, so a request is answered from memory in one step; only a miss pays for a resize, and only a missing original ends in not found.
lede: This covers the path of one request from arrival to answer, the three outcomes it can reach, and the one delay that can surprise a caller.

sections.title: One request, start to finish
sections.summary: A request either finds its thumbnail in the cache, or it is resized from the origin store and kept for next time.
sections.what: Every request names an image and a size. The service looks in its cache first. On a miss it reads the original from the origin store, resizes it and keeps the result.
sections.why: Resizing is the slow part. Keeping each result means the second request for the same size costs a lookup, not a resize.
sections.how: The lookup key is the image name plus the requested width, built in [[router.py:18]]. The resize step lives in [[resize.py:30]] and writes its result back before answering, so two requests for the same new size do the work once. The code that names the step is `cache.put`.

sections.title: The three answers a caller can get
sections.summary: Every request ends in exactly one of three answers, and each one is decided by a single line of code.
sections.what: A caller sees a status, a body and a header that says where the image came from.
sections.why: Callers use the source header to tell a fresh resize from a cached copy when they measure speed.

sections.title: Inside the cache: room and staleness
sections.summary: The cache holds a fixed number of thumbnails; when it is full, eviction removes the one used longest ago.
sections.what: Room is counted in thumbnails, not bytes. A full cache makes room before it stores a new copy.
sections.why: Counting thumbnails keeps the rule simple to reason about, at the price of uneven memory use.
sections.how: The limit is read once at start-up in [[cache.py:12]]. Eviction runs inside the same call that stores, so the count never goes over the limit.

components.title: Watch out
components.body: A copy can be served for up to ten minutes after its original changes, because stored copies are not checked against the origin store on every request.

components.title: Good to know
components.body: Misses are counted separately, so a sudden rise in resizes shows up as its own number.

claims.claim: The lookup key is the image name plus the requested width.
A stored copy is served without touching the origin store.
A resize writes its result back before answering.
A missing original ends in status 404 with an empty body.
Copies can be up to ten minutes stale after the original changes.
